scenes.text: [mischievously] Your Stripe secret key was hiding in plain sight, inside your public JavaScript. Claude spotted it.
It lived in an env var starting with Vite underscore, and Vite pastes those values straight into the browser bundle.
So anyone could open view source, search the minified code, and walk off with your Stripe account.
Claude moved the payment call to a server route, so the secret never leaves it. The browser only gets the publishable key.
Then it rotated the leaked key, because once a secret ships, it's stolen.
If it starts with Vite, the whole internet can read it.
